args.body:
Hi Dora! Thanks for the invite — welcome to Slack. I took a look at your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and straightforward — the page loads fast and gets straight to the point about who you are.
- The site feels personal and authentic, which is a nice touch for a personal website.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add a bit more substance: a short intro about who you are, what you do, or what you're interested in. Right now the site is very sparse, so visitors don't get much to latch onto.
- Consider adding a few sections such as a portfolio of your work, a blog, or a list of projects you've been involved in.
- Add links to your other profiles (GitHub, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, etc.) so people can connect with you elsewhere.
- A small bit of visual design — some color, a header image, or a personal photo — would help the site feel more finished and memorable.
- Include a way to get in touch beyond just an email address, like a contact form or a social link.

Overall, it's a nice starting point and very easy to read. With a little more content and personality, it could go a long way. Nice work!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I had a look at your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to send along some feedback.

What I liked:
- The blog has a warm, personal feel — it reads like it's written by a real person, which is exactly what makes a blog worth following.
- Hiking is a fantastic subject to write about. It's a topic with a lot of genuine enthusiasm behind it, and readers can sense that.
- The site is simple and loads quickly, so there's nothing standing between a visitor and your writing.

Suggestions to make it even stronger:
- Add a few actual blog posts. Right now the site is mostly a landing page, so there's not much for a new reader to dig into. Even one or two well-written entries would give people a reason to come back.
- Consider organizing posts by topic or trail, and adding a short intro that tells readers what your blog is about.
- Photos are huge for a hiking blog — adding images from your adventures would make it far more engaging and shareable.
- Add an archive or "latest posts" list, plus a way for readers to subscribe (RSS, newsletter, or social links).
- A short bio and a contact method would help readers connect with you and get in touch.

Overall, the foundation is nice and the subject matter is genuinely appealing. With a bit more published content and some visuals, it could become a really enjoyable read. Looking forward to seeing more posts!

Best,
Emma Johnson
